olga: Observed flaky behavior in the Android Kotlin sample: when we do token refresh inside an OkHttp Authenticator, bursts of concurrent requests trigger multiple refreshes and some sockets later throw SocketException.

nate: Can you repro? which OS/emulator?

olga: Pixel 6 emulator Android 12, run 8 concurrent POSTs to /v1/embeddings with auth stub delaying refresh by 2.5s. After a few runs we see: 
```
I/OkHttp: <-- 401 https://api.redwood/v1/embeddings
I/Auth: refreshing token (req=abc)
I/OkHttp: <-- 401 https://api.redwood/v1/embeddings
W/OkHttp: stream allocation still active
E/OkHttp: java.net.SocketException: Socket closed
```

min: Two things: 1) Authenticator executes on network threads and can cause duplicate refreshes. 2) If calls time out while waiting, canceled calls can leave streams open.

nate: Workarounds?

min: Move refresh into an application interceptor and gate using a Mutex/singleflight. Also ensure you close ResponseBody in all paths (use `.use {}` or `response.close()`). For retries, avoid `call.clone()` when the original may be canceled; create a fresh `client.newCall(newRequest)` instead.

olga: I switched to interceptor with a coroutine Mutex and retry-once. That eliminated duplicate refreshes. I also added `connectionPool.evictAll()` when rotating tokens in the sample; seemed to help on emulator.

qa-bot: tests/sampleapp-android #91 flake reproduced (see logs)

nate: Let's add a short note to devex: "Android SDK: avoid heavy work in OkHttp Authenticator; prefer app-managed refresh with singleflight; always close responses; prefer newCall over clone when cancellation possible; consider evictAll() on token rotation."

min: I'll draft a sample code snippet for the docs. olga, can you open a small PR with the mutex pattern and the evictAll change to the sampleapp?

olga: Yep, opening PR now and will include repro steps and an annotated log snippet. :+1:
